Question: Assume \(0 \lt r \lt 3.\) Below are five equations for \(x.\) Which equation has the largest solution \(x?\)
Solution:
Dividing each equation by \(3\) gives an equation of the form \(b^x=7/3\), where \(b>1\). Each has a unique positive solution. At a fixed positive exponent, a larger base gives a larger value, so the smallest base requires the largest exponent to reach \(7/3\).

We therefore compare the quantities added to \(1\). Since \(r>0\),
\[
\frac r{10}<r<2r.
\]
Also, \(r<3<100\) gives
\[
\left(\frac r{10}\right)^2=\frac{r^2}{100}<r.
\]
Both quantities being compared are positive, so \(r/10<\sqrt r\). Finally, \(r^2<9<10\); dividing by the positive number \(10r\) gives \(r/10<1/r\).

Thus \(1+r/10\) is strictly smaller than all four other bases. Its equation has the largest solution, so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
